findings.title: Keep approvals retryable after handler storage failures
findings.why_it_matters: A transient database failure inside a confirmed recruitment handler can permanently consume the owner's approval even though the purchase was rolled back. The executor converts that storage exception into a handler failure, and the confirmation path commits a terminal failed receipt. A later execute request only returns that terminal receipt, so recovery requires a new proposal and approval; this contradicts the explicit retryability rule for storage failures.
evidence: apps/server/app/work/action_confirmations.py:370-385: the savepoint comment says a storage failure must leave approval retryable, but any result without audit_id is finalized as failed and other handler failures reach row.status = "failed".

apps/server/app/work/tool_executor.py:863-896: every non-ToolError raised by spec.handler is caught, rolled back to the savepoint, converted to handler_failed, then returned as a normal failure result.
apps/server/app/work/action_confirmations.py:357-371: terminal confirmations return without execution; approved is the only executable state.
apps/server/app/work/tool_recruitment.py:32-38: confirmed recruitment invokes the M1/T2 purchase path with commit=False inside that handler.

/var/folders/qb/xn8nq_t53rz276g17td9yts40000gn/T/eidolon-m3-3-close-2z9plmwf/review-fault-red-configured.log: injected INSERT failures for employees and events are logged as handler_failed rather than escaping as an OperationalError.
findings.suggested_fix: Let SQLAlchemy storage exceptions from the tool handler escape the executor's generic handler-failure conversion, so the outer confirmation transaction rolls back and retains status approved. Continue recording explicit domain rejections as terminal failures. Extend the confirmation fault-injection test to fail a recruitment domain or source-event write once, then verify unchanged approval, no effects or final receipt, and successful replay after recovery.
findings.validation_reason: On reviewed HEAD 5f8db04, an approved recruitment encountering a transient handler storage error reaches tool_executor.py:869-896, which rolls back the handler savepoint and returns handler_failed; the newly introduced action_confirmations.py:385-390 then commits failed, and lines 357-359 prevent replay, while the supplied review-fault-red-configured.log independently demonstrates reachable employee/event INSERT fault paths with OperationalError swallowed, unlike the final-audit-only coverage at test_m3_action_confirmations.py:464-490 (production incidence was not measured).

residual_risks.title: Clean up worker streams when telemetry persistence fails
residual_risks.risk: If telemetry observation fails after a real worker starts, the exception path finalizes and releases the work session but does not cancel or await the adapter-owned producer task. The adapters create that producer separately and their stream iterators do not clean it up, so the remote run may continue after ownership is released.
evidence: apps/server/app/workflow/orchestrator.py:463-475: this exception path finalizes the failed host session without producer cleanup.
apps/server/app/runtimes/hermes/adapter.py:118-120 and apps/server/app/runtimes/openclaw/adapter.py:127-129: adapters create session.background with asyncio.create_task.
residual_risks.suggested_response: Cancel and await the producer task, then make a bounded run-targeted cancellation attempt before releasing worker ownership; add an observe-failure test.
residual_risks.disposition: Retained as a residual risk by synthesis; not selected for independent validation. Parent supplied a failing worker-cleanup reproduction.
